Report_ID: Change in serum ferritin (Δ SF) from baseline to study end (µg/L): FeSO4+citrate-fortified fish sauce vs placebo fish sauce
Title: A comparative intervention trial on fish sauce fortified with NaFe-EDTA and FeSO4+citrate in iron deficiency anemic school children in Kampot, Cambodia
Author: Longfils et al.
Comment: End-of-study SF values are reported only as geometric means with 25th/75th percentiles (placebo 12.2 [6.5, 19.8] n=44; FeSO4+citrate 20.4 [12.0, 33.1] n=47), so CHANGE SCORES (mean ± SD of Δ SF) were used for both arms as specified by the plan. p-value shown is the paper's pairwise comparison 1-2 reported as p<0.01 (entered as 0.01, an upper bound). M_diff computed as group_2_mean − group_1_mean from the two explicitly reported arm means. Table 1 header states 'n = 164', inconsistent with the 137 analysed subjects; per-cell n values were used. Three-arm trial: the placebo arm is shared with the NaFe-EDTA row.
Participant type: iron-deficiency anaemic school children and adolescents aged 6–21 years
Recruitment source: Hun Sen High School and a nearby primary school, Chhuk district, Kampot province
Outcome measurement: Δ SF (µg/L), mean ± SD, baseline to end of 21-week intervention
Outcome variable: Change in serum ferritin (Δ SF) from baseline to study end (µg/L): FeSO4+citrate-fortified fish sauce vs placebo fish sauce
additional_group_ns: Third arm not used in this row: NaFe-EDTA-fortified fish sauce, Δ SF 17.3 ± 14.7 (n=46) — extracted as a separate row

Report_ID: Plasma (serum) ferritin concentration at 1 year (males 19–54 yr subgroup)
Title: Studies on the effectiveness of NaFeEDTA-fortified soy sauce in controlling iron deficiency: A population-based intervention trial
Author: Chen J, Zhao X, Zhang X, Yin S, Piao J, Huo J, Yu B, Qu N, Lu Q, Wang S, Chen C
Comment: (1) Ferritin means are GEOMETRIC means: values were log-transformed then antilog-transformed, so the reported "± SD" is not a straightforward arithmetic SD on the µg/L scale; no arithmetic mean/SD is given by the paper. (2) Table 4 reports ferritin only by age/sex subgroup — no overall trial total is reported; one representative subgroup row was recorded and all other subgroups are listed in additional_group_ns (they comprise non-overlapping participants of the same trial). (3) Trial was randomised by village (cluster-randomised: 5 fortified villages / 4 control villages) but NO ICC or design effect is reported and no cluster-adjusted analysis is presented, so sample sizes could not be adjusted for clustering — the recorded Ns are the unadjusted analysed Ns. (4) Last ferritin follow-up is 12 months (ferritin was not measured at 18 months). (5) p-value recorded as the table's "***" vs control (p<.001); exact p not reported. (6) M_diff deliberately left empty because the means are anti-logged (geometric) values, so a raw difference would be on an ambiguous scale. (7) Units already µg/L (=ng/mL); no conversion applied.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Fortified group (NaFeEDTA-fortified soy sauce), males 19–54 yr, 1 yr') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Content length: 18-month intervention; ferritin measured at baseline and 12 months
Participant type: Rural residents aged ≥3 years (children, adults, elderly) in Haizijie Town, Bijie City, Guizhou Province, China
Recruitment source: Nine villages in the Haizijie Region, Bijie City, Guizhou Province; evaluation cohort sampled via school classes and their whole households (~1/3 of population)
Outcome measurement: Mean ± SD (µg/L) at 1 year, fortified vs control soy sauce group
Outcome variable: Plasma (serum) ferritin concentration at 1 year (males 19–54 yr subgroup)
additional_group_ns: Other age/sex subgroups at 1 yr (fortified vs control, mean ± SD, n): males 7–18 yr 6.18±2.05 (352) vs 5.05±2.55 (389), p<.01; males 55+ yr 8.44±2.55 (64) vs 9.51±2.51 (62); females 7–18 yr 5.67±2.22 (284) vs 4.74±2.66 (301), p<.05; females 19–30 yr 4.45±2.96 (118) vs 3.59±3.05 (127); females 31–54 yr 5.04±2.51 (349) vs 4.52±2.78 (392); females 55+ yr 8.46±2.60 (73) vs 8.97±2.53 (65). 3–6 yr children had no ferritin measurement (capillary blood, hemoglobin only).

Report_ID: Serum ferritin (µg/L) after 2 y of fortification — males
Title: Fortification of curry powder with NaFe(III)EDTA in an iron-deficient population: report of a controlled iron-fortification trial
Author: Ballot DE, MacPhail AP, Bothwell TH, Gillooly M, Mayet FG
Comment: Ferritin is reported ONLY as a geometric mean with a one-SD RANGE (fortified males 56, range 20–159; control males 39, range 13–122) — no arithmetic mean or arithmetic SD is given, so no SD could be recorded; geometric means entered per plan and noted. The p = 0.04 (one-tailed Student's t test) refers to the CHANGE in ferritin from baseline being greater in the fortified group, not to a test of end-of-study means. Allocation was by family (cluster-like) with no ICC reported, so no design-effect adjustment of n was possible. n per arm are the year-2 analysed numbers from Table 2.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Fortified masala (NaFe(III)EDTA), males') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Design Type: double-blind randomised controlled fortification trial (allocation by family)
Participant type: South African Indian community members aged ≥10 y (males)
Recruitment source: Subeconomic housing area, Chatsworth, near Durban
Outcome measurement: Geometric mean serum ferritin concentration at year 2 (end of intervention)
Outcome variable: Serum ferritin (µg/L) after 2 y of fortification — males

Report_ID: Serum ferritin (SF) — change from baseline (t0) to 6 mo (t6)
Title: Regular consumption of NaFeEDTA-fortified fish sauce improves iron status and reduces the prevalence of anemia in anemic Vietnamese women
Author: Pham Van Thuy; Jacques Berger; Lena Davidsson; Nguyen Cong Khan; Nguyen Thi Lam; James D Cook; Richard F Hurrell; Ha Huy Khoi
Comment: Change-from-baseline scores (mean ± SD) used for BOTH arms because end-of-intervention ferritin is reported only as geometric means with 95% CI (iron-fortified 30.9 [23.4, 40.6]; control 14.6 [11.3, 19.0] µg/L), with no arithmetic mean/SD available. P value reported as "< 0.0001" (recorded as 0.0001, an upper bound). Units already µg/L, no conversion needed. "±" denotes SD per Table 2 footnote 2 ("x̄ ± SD"). M_diff not computed to avoid sign ambiguity (group_1 is the treatment arm); difference of change means = 18.7 − 2.8 = 15.9 µg/L favouring fortification. Individually randomised (not cluster-randomised); no ICC adjustment required. Abstract states P = 0.0002 for t6 SF whereas Table 2 footnote states P = 0.0006 (internal discrepancy).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Iron-fortified group (10 mL/d fish sauce with 10 mg Fe as NaFeEDTA)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Content length: 6 mo intervention (26–28 wk), fish sauce served 6 d/wk
Topic of Content: NaFeEDTA-fortified fish sauce for control of iron deficiency anemia
Participant type: anemic nonpregnant women aged 17–49 y (factory workers), hemoglobin 81–119 g/L
Recruitment source: 6 factories in Hai Duong and Hung Yen provinces, Red River delta, northern Vietnam (screening of 2159 women)
Outcome measurement: Mean change in serum ferritin concentration from baseline to 6 mo, µg/L (end-of-intervention values reported only as geometric means with 95% CI: 30.9 [23.4, 40.6] vs 14.6 [11.3, 19.0] µg/L, P = 0.0006)
Outcome variable: Serum ferritin (SF) — change from baseline (t0) to 6 mo (t6)

Report_ID: Serum ferritin (SF) after 3 months of intervention — low-NaFeEDTA fortified soy sauce vs non-fortified soy sauce
Title: Therapeutic effects of NaFeEDTA-fortified soy sauce in anaemic children in China
Author: Huo et al.
Comment: P-value shown is the paper's threshold (P<0.01) for the comparison with control (footnote bb), not an exact value. M_diff computed as group_2_mean − group_1_mean from the two explicitly reported end-of-intervention means. Units ng/mL = µg/L, no conversion needed. Allocation was effectively by school (cluster-type); no ICC reported, so no design-effect adjustment was applied. The Results text mistakenly writes 'SI' where SF vs control is described.
Participant type: anaemic boarding school children aged 11–17 years
Recruitment source: Three middle schools, Wancheng District, Nanyang City, Henan Province, China
Outcome measurement: End-of-intervention (3-month) arithmetic mean ± SD serum ferritin
Outcome variable: Serum ferritin (SF) after 3 months of intervention — low-NaFeEDTA fortified soy sauce vs non-fortified soy sauce
additional_group_ns: High NaFeEDTA group (4 mg Fe/mL, ~20 mg Fe/day), n=77 analysed — recorded as a separate row (E2); assigned Ns were 102 control, 102 low, 100 high

Title: The Use of NaFeEDTA-Fortified Fish Sauce Is an Effective Tool for Controlling Iron Deficiency in Women of Childbearing Age in Rural Vietnam
Author: Pham Van Thuy; Jacques Berger; Yukiko Nakanishi; Nguyen Cong Khan; Sean Lynch; Philip Dixon
Comment: Ferritin reported ONLY as GEOMETRIC means with 95% CI after log transformation; no arithmetic mean or SD is given, so SD could not be extracted or validly computed (and the CI is on the back-transformed log scale, so an SD derived from it would be invalid). End-of-intervention (T18) values used, not change scores. Units already µg/L (=ng/mL); no conversion applied. Cluster-randomised by village (21 villages, median 25 women/village): the paper states intraclass correlation coefficients were computed but reports NO numeric ICC, so no design-effect adjustment of n could be made; the Ns given (190 and 199) are the analysed Ns from the paper's own village-adjusted linear mixed model. P-value recorded as the reported threshold "<0.001". M_diff not computed because the means are geometric means from a log-transformed mixed model, not simple arithmetic group means.; treatment SD derived from its reported mean CI; control SD derived from its reported mean CI
Design Type: cluster-randomised double-blind controlled trial (randomisation by village)
Study Environment: community / field setting (household-level free distribution of fish sauce, 18 mo)
Topic of Content: NaFeEDTA-fortified fish sauce for control of iron deficiency
Participant type: Nonpregnant women of childbearing age (16–49 y) in rural villages
Recruitment source: Randomly selected households with at least one nonpregnant woman aged 16–49 y in 21 villages of 2 communes, Vu Ban district, Nam Dinh province, Red River Delta, Vietnam
Outcome measurement: Geometric mean serum ferritin (µg/L) with 95% CI, after log transformation; linear mixed model with village variance component
